verdict.label: Light review
verdict.summary: Create a Slack app via the developer portal or Slack CLI, configure OAuth redirect URLs, and connect it through Composio.

composioFit.summary: Composio provides a managed OAuth app for Slack out of the box, but you can bring your own custom OAuth app for dedicated rate limits, custom branding, and custom scopes.
whyOwnApp: Dedicated provider rate limits instead of sharing with other Composio customers
Request custom scopes beyond what Composio's default managed app requests

phases.name: Create Slack App
steps: Go to the Slack App Management page or use the Slack CLI to create a new app.
Configure basic information such as app name and icon.
phases.handoff: Slack App ID and Client Credentials

phases.name: Configure OAuth and Redirect URIs
steps: Navigate to OAuth & Permissions in your Slack app settings.
Add your HTTPS Redirect URIs matching the Composio callback URL.
Configure required bot and user scopes.

phases.name: Test Integration
steps: Initiate the OAuth flow using the authorization URL.
Approve scopes in your Slack workspace and exchange the temporary code for an access token via oauth.v2.access.

artefacts.body: Our AI agent requests chat:write and commands scopes to send messages and execute commands on behalf of the user within their authorized Slack workspace.

requirements.label: Privacy Policy URL
requirements.when: Required when distributing your app publicly or listing on the Slack Marketplace.

scopes.purpose: Post messages to specific channels via incoming webhooks.
Add slash commands to the workspace.
Send messages on behalf of the app.
Non-Enterprise scope that cannot be installed on Enterprise orgs.

redirectRules.rule: A Redirect URL can not contain an anchor (#).
Your redirect_uri must match or be a subdirectory of a Redirect URL configured under App Management.

blockers.cause: Occurs when there are multiple redirect_url parameter values configured and they do not match between steps.
blockers.fix: Ensure the redirect_uri parameter is sent in both the Authorize and Access steps with the exact same value.
blockers.fallback: Configure a single Redirect URL in App Management.

blockers.cause: Occurs if requesting a non-existent scope or requesting a set of scopes that are in conflict with each other (e.g., SIWS user scopes combined with non-SIWS user scopes).
blockers.fix: Separate Sign in with Slack user scopes from non-Sign in with Slack scopes into separate OAuth flows.
blockers.fallback: Remove conflicting scopes from the request.

blockers.cause: Occurs when attempting to install/authorize an undistributed Slack API app on a team where the app was not created.
blockers.fix: Install the app directly on the workspace that owns it, or distribute the app.
blockers.fallback: Use the home workspace for development and testing.

blockers.cause: Occurs when attempting to install an app in an Enterprise org containing scopes that are not org-compatible.
blockers.fix: Remove non-Enterprise compatible scopes like 'bot' from your enterprise app configuration.
blockers.fallback: Install on a standard single workspace instead of an Enterprise org.

checklist.text: Create your Slack app via App Management or the Slack CLI.
Configure valid HTTPS Redirect URIs in OAuth & Permissions.
Select required bot and user permission scopes.
Implement the OAuth authorization code flow redirect and token exchange.

uncertainties: Exact marketplace review turnaround time is not explicitly documented in the provided source text.
Specific pricing tiers for paid Slack developer plans are not detailed in the excerpts.
